decision.argument_basis: scope evidence not reflected in the mapping
decision.evidence_cited: The role summary describes end-to-end, unsupervised ownership of a full analog block (bandgap reference and LDO regulator) through a complete tapeout with first-pass silicon success, explicitly framed as individual contributor scope with the block "owned end to end." Nyx's own anchor for MTS I (section 4) describes work "within an established area under a more senior engineer's direction," contributing "a defined piece of a larger block rather than owning one outright," with "supervised sign-off." That does not match the described scope at all -- there is no mention of supervision or partial ownership. The described scope instead matches Nyx's own MTS II anchor: "Owns a component or sub-block independently, start to finish... Full, unsupervised ownership of at least one tapeout-scale piece of work, still within a single area." The current MTS I level appears to be a title/record artifact (section 3 warns titles are not self-executing) rather than a re-read of the actual scope, and Meridian's proposed L3 mapping seems to have carried that MTS I label forward without accounting for the unsupervised, full-block ownership described in the summary.
decision.framework_section: Section 4 (Level anchors: MTS I vs. MTS II) and Section 3 (Leveling principle -- title is not self-executing)
